items.followUp: Differentiate between a cation and an anion.

rubric.why: Shows that an ion carries an electrical charge.
rubric.description: Defines an ion as a charged atom or group of atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an ion has a charge.

rubric.why: Identifies the distinguishing feature of a free radical.
rubric.description: Defines a free radical as an atom or group of atoms containing one or more unpaired electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning an unpaired electron in an atom or group of atoms.

modelAnswer: An ion is an atom or group of atoms that carries a positive or negative charge.
A free radical is an atom or group of atoms containing one or more unpaired electrons.

items.followUp: Why is air considered a mixture?

rubric.why: Names substances present in a soft drink, showing it contains more than one component.
rubric.description: Identifies two or more components of a soft drink.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving examples of different components, such as water, sugar and carbon dioxide.

rubric.why: Explains why the components form a mixture rather than a compound.
rubric.description: States that the components are physically mixed, not chemically combined, and/or that their proportions can vary.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of the mixture.

modelAnswer: A soft drink contains several substances, such as water, sugar, carbon dioxide and flavouring.
These substances are physically mixed, not chemically combined, and their proportions can vary; therefore, a soft drink is a mixture.

items.followUp: How many protons and neutrons are present in tritium, ³₁H?

rubric.why: Deuterium has atomic number 1, so its nucleus contains one proton.
rubric.description: Gives the number of protons in deuterium.

rubric.why: The mass number is 2 and the atomic number is 1, so neutrons = 2 − 1 = 1.
rubric.description: Gives the number of neutrons in deuterium.

modelAnswer: Deuterium is ²₁H, so its atomic number is 1 and its mass number is 2.
Number of neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 2 − 1 = 1.

items.followUp: Write the subshell electronic configuration of aluminium (Al), atomic number 13.

rubric.why: Magnesium has atomic number 12, so a neutral atom has 12 electrons to place in subshells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating or correctly using 12 electrons.

rubric.why: Confirms the electrons are filled in the correct subshells for magnesium.
rubric.description: Gives the complete subshell electronic configuration of magnesium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct configuration.

modelAnswer: Magnesium has atomic number 12, so a neutral Mg atom has 12 electrons.
Filling the subshells in order gives: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s².

items.followUp: How many elements are present in the first and fourth periods of the modern periodic table?

rubric.description: States that the second and third periods are the normal periods.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly naming both periods.

rubric.why: Gives the number of elements in each normal period.
rubric.description: States that each normal period contains eight elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating eight elements in each.

modelAnswer: The second and third periods are the normal periods.

items.followUp: Define covalent radius and state a commonly used unit for atomic radius.

rubric.why: Describes the textbook measure of an atom's size.
rubric.description: Defines atomic radius as the distance from the centre of the nucleus to the outermost electron shell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the distance from the nucleus/centre to the outermost shell.

rubric.why: Provides an accepted unit for atomic radius.
rubric.description: States a unit of atomic radius.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for nm, pm or angstrom.

modelAnswer: Atomic radius is the distance from the centre of an atom's nucleus to its outermost electron shell.
It is commonly expressed in nanometres (nm).

items.followUp: What is the trend of electron affinity across a period from left to right?

rubric.why: States the general periodic trend in ionization energy.
rubric.description: States that ionization energy generally increases from left to right across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct increasing trend.

rubric.why: Provides a valid reason for the increase in ionization energy across a period.
rubric.description: Explains the trend in terms of increasing nuclear attraction and/or decreasing atomic radius.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy generally increases from left to right across a period.
The nuclear charge increases while electrons are added to the same shell, so the attraction between the nucleus and outer electrons becomes stronger.

rubric.why: States the defining number of elements in a Dobereiner triad.
rubric.description: Defines a triad as a group of three elements with similar chemical properties, arranged in order of increasing atomic mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying three similar elements arranged by increasing atomic mass.

rubric.why: States the relationship between the atomic mass of the middle element and the other two.
rubric.description: States that the atomic mass of the middle element is approximately the arithmetic mean of the other two.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the approximate mean relationship.

modelAnswer: Dobereiner's triads are groups of three elements with similar chemical properties, arranged in order of increasing atomic mass.
The atomic mass of the middle element is approximately the arithmetic mean of the atomic masses of the other two elements.
